publisher: Notary Geek / GoodWare LLC / Greg Lirette
scope: Partial California routes: county no-record procurement, CDPH unsuccessful-search results and private single-status affidavits; public/confidential marriage records; SOS company records; Superior Court divorce/judgment certification; issuer-prepared education records. Exact output/signer gaps and recipient acceptance remain explicit.
coreQuestion: Whose signature is on the actual California document, and is the output an original or qualifying certified record for California Secretary of State authentication?

routeFacts.claim: The California Secretary of State authenticates California public officials' signatures for documents used outside the United States; its apostille confirms the signature, capacity, and seal when applicable, not the document's contents.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-guidance
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Request page introduction; FAQ 1

routeFacts.claim: California says it issues a single Apostille for documents used outside the United States regardless of destination country. That state output does not establish whether any receiving-country or consular step remains for a non-Convention destination.
routeFacts.evidence: agency statement plus Notary Geek destination-route inference
routeFacts.sourceLocator: FAQ 2; HCCH status table (retained September 29 source date)
routeFacts.sourceFreshnessLimit: California FAQ refreshed; treaty status retained from September 29 and must be checked for actual destination/date.

routeFacts.claim: A mailed document must bear a California public official signature or be an original notarized and/or certified document; photocopies are unacceptable. Mail requests go through Sacramento, with a destination-country cover sheet, $20 per Apostille, and a self-addressed return envelope.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-procedure
routeFacts.sourceLocator: How to Request an Apostille by Mail, items 1–4

routeFacts.claim: The Secretary of State gives different Sacramento addresses for USPS and other carriers and says prepaid tracking postage is needed for tracked return; without it, the office returns by regular USPS mail. Sending overnight does not expedite processing after receipt.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-procedure
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Mail carrier addresses and return postage; FAQ 7

routeFacts.claim: Sacramento and Los Angeles offer in-person same-day service, with a $20 Apostille fee plus a $6 special handling charge for each different public official's signature authenticated. The $6 charge applies to in-person requests, not mail; it is not necessarily $6 per document.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-procedure
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Sacramento and Los Angeles in-person instructions; FAQ 6

routeFacts.claim: For birth and death records, directly recognizable signatures include county clerks/deputies, county recorders/deputies, and State Registrar. A city/county health officer or local registrar signature may require county clerk certification or a newly issued certified copy from the county recorder or California Department of Public Health.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-document-specific-guidance
routeFacts.sourceLocator: FAQ 3

routeFacts.claim: Checked October 28, 2026: the SOS page, updated October 27, reported processing apostille mail received October 16. Counter processing was typically within 30 minutes, with arrival by 4:30 p.m. advised. These are dated agency observations, not an end-to-end deadline.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-dated-operational-status
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Apostilles / Mail / In Person; displayed update October 27, 2026

routeFacts.claim: The Los Angeles office currently flags temporary first-floor suite 1215 service due to an elevator outage while its general address remains Room 12513; mail is not accepted there. Confirm the current counter location before visiting.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-operational-notice
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Los Angeles temporary-service notice; Tips for Submission

routeFacts.claim: California SOS offers online certified copies and certificates of status for corporations, LLCs and LPs, while plain online printouts are a different, free category. A public-company record route starts with the actual SOS certification and official signature rather than a plain image or private custodian statement.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-records guidance plus Notary Geek signature-route inference
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Certificates, Copies, Status Reports and Processing Times

routeFacts.claim: For certified copies of filed entity records outside corporations, LLCs and LPs, California says the request must be on paper and the Business Programs Division's copy carries a manually placed certification stamp with date, Secretary signature, State seal, page count and deputy initials.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-records guidance
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Note below Plain Copies

routeFacts.claim: The state says bylaws and operating agreements are maintained by the entity rather than filed with California SOS; their notarial signature route is distinct from an SOS-issued company certificate. Its online availability of a certified copy does not by itself establish that a self-printed output is acceptable for a mailed apostille, which requires an original/certified document and rejects photocopies.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency facts plus Notary Geek output-lane inference
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Frequently Requested Information / Bylaws or Operating Agreements

routeFacts.claim: The March 2026 paper order form includes Corp/LLC/LP/GP/LLP choices, certified filings and status certificates. Certified copies cost $5 per document; status certificates $5 each. Sacramento handles paper requests; mail orders return by mail; drop-off offers mail or pickup and a separate $10 per-entity handling fee. These are record-order charges, separate from apostille fees.
routeFacts.evidence: official-agency-guidance
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Form p1 items 1–4; p2 items 1/3/4; p3 Fees and Where to Submit

routeFacts.claim: Online certification and verification are documented, but the reviewed public instructions do not specify whether an unaltered customer printout of that certified output is accepted for a paper apostille, or needs agency paper certification. No acceptance or rejection of that exact output is established. A verification code alone does not resolve presentation.
routeFacts.evidence: Notary Geek bounded evidence-gap finding
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Business Records; Certified Copies (Online); apostille mail item 1

routeFacts.claim: The published paper order route can obtain an agency-issued certified record instead of relying on a customer printout. Preserve its complete certification, signature and seal, then use SOS apostille submission instructions for that actual output. The other-entity manual-stamp description must not be generalized to the form of every Corp/LLC/LP paper certificate.
routeFacts.evidence: Notary Geek route synthesis from official procedures
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Paper order form; other-entity stamp note; apostille mail item 1

routeFacts.claim: UC Davis requires newly generated original transcripts/verifications; diploma requests instead use a copy authenticated and notarized through its Registrar. Berkeley likewise offers registrar notarization and identifies the California notary signature as the apostille target. These are institution-specific routes, not a statewide direct-registrar-signature rule.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: UC Davis Documents Available for Notarization; Berkeley Apostilles
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer-procedure

routeFacts.claim: Caltech publishes a registrar certifying cover letter, notarization, and mailing to SOS with return to the requester. Use its Procedure for issuer preparation only; its opening description of apostille as true-copy certification does not displace SOS FAQ 1. No individual signer or specimen certificate was inspected.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Caltech Procedure; SOS FAQ 1
routeFacts.evidence: issuer procedure plus Notary Geek source-conflict resolution

routeFacts.claim: The 2026 SOS handbook reproduces limited notary copy-certification authority, including powers of attorney, not general authority to certify diploma copies. Its tangible electronic-copy procedure under Government Code 27201.1 uses a custodian statement and jurat for recording; it does not establish an issuer-certified academic record or apostille printout eligibility.
routeFacts.evidence: official handbook/statutory text plus Notary Geek scope inference

routeFacts.claim: A student or custodian statement notarized in California can only be described as that private statement: the apostille concerns the notary signature. It is not the registrar-certified transcript or diploma, even when attached to a copy. Recipient acceptance of a substitute must be separately established.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: SOS FAQ 1; Berkeley Apostilles; handbook copy-certification provisions
routeFacts.evidence: Notary Geek signature-route inference

routeFacts.claim: The divorce decree/judgment comes from the originating Superior Court. CDPH only holds a 1962–June 1984 Certificate of Record, not the decree; the CDC directory clarifies that this record does not establish finality. CDPH was available as official indexed text, with direct retrieval unsuccessful.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: CDPH opening paragraphs; CDC Divorce State/County
routeFacts.evidence: official issuer statement corroborated by federal directory; access limit

routeFacts.claim: Orange County describes a certified copy as bearing a dated Deputy Clerk signature and court seal/stamp; its exemplification is a separate document-listing form prepared by a deputy and signed by a Superior Court judge. A possible foreign-recipient request for exemplification is not a stated statewide SOS prerequisite.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Orange FAQ p2; SOS FAQ 1
routeFacts.evidence: court procedure plus Notary Geek boundary inference

routeFacts.claim: Stanislaus optional G003 (Rev 02/04), still listed in its official forms catalog, shows deputy-clerk copy attestation/seal, judge authentication of the deputy, then deputy-clerk authentication of the judge/seal. These are Superior Court officials, not an assumed County Clerk step. Indexed form text is an example, not a mandatory apostille chain.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: G003 three certificate blocks; catalog Civil/Family Law
routeFacts.evidence: official court form via search index; bounded example

routeFacts.claim: Orange County allows certified-copy orders and describes mailed delivery for online, mail and telephone requests. Mail orders require document identification, payment and an addressed postage-paid envelope; restricted records retain access conditions. Online ordering does not establish self-printed court-document eligibility.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Requesting Copies / Copies of Documents
routeFacts.evidence: court procedure plus Notary Geek output inference

routeFacts.claim: Orange County sources conflict: its undated copy FAQ says processing/mailing within 1–3 court days; its Family Law Records page says 30–45 days. No turnaround promise is adopted; confirm current issuer processing before relying on either.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: FAQ p1 first question; Records page online/mail copy order guidance
routeFacts.evidence: unresolved official-source conflict

routeFacts.claim: Business filing electronic/digital signature instructions govern filings submitted to SOS; they are not instructions approving or rejecting customer-printed SOS-certified outputs for apostille.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Business FAQ Electronic Signatures / Digital Signatures; apostille mail item 1
routeFacts.evidence: Notary Geek source-scope inference

routeFacts.claim: Public marriage records follow the County Recorder in the county where the license was issued; confidential records follow that county Clerk. Ceremony location alone does not select the custodian. Obtain the registered record, not merely an uncompleted license or an application.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Directory / Marriage Records; San Diego opening and registration FAQ
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer-guidance plus Notary Geek document-identity distinction

routeFacts.claim: CDPH does not hold confidential marriages. Its dedicated public-marriage page lists 1905–1999, 2001 and 2008–2025, whereas FAQ 8 lists 1905–1999 and 2008–2023. These indexed observations differ. Confirm the event year or use the license-issuing county; neither an omitted year nor a failed search proves no marriage exists.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Dedicated page opening; FAQ 8
routeFacts.evidence: official indexed guidance with unresolved availability discrepancy

routeFacts.claim: Authorized and informational public-marriage copies are both certified, but an informational copy cannot establish identity. Confidential copies are restricted to a party to the marriage or court order; no informational confidential copy is issued. Sacramento cites HSC 103526 and Family Code 509/511 for these distinctions.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Opening; Public Marriage Records; Confidential Marriage Records
routeFacts.evidence: official-county-guidance citing statute; current code text not directly retrieved

routeFacts.claim: SOS permits third-party in-person apostille submission. That permission does not expand eligibility to obtain a confidential marriage certificate. A courier or relative must not borrow the public-record authorized-person list to obtain a confidential record.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: SOS FAQ 5; Sacramento Confidential Marriage Records
routeFacts.evidence: Notary Geek inference separating access from submission

routeFacts.claim: The notarized statement used to request an authorized copy establishes the applicant request, not certification of the issued marriage record. San Diego allows an out-of-California notary venue on that application. The resulting California record follows its issuing official signature, not the application notary state.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: San Diego By Mail; SOS introduction
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer procedure plus Notary Geek signature-route inference

routeFacts.claim: San Mateo expressly permits its County Clerk-Recorder-issued marriage certificate to go directly to SOS without additional documentation. This supports that issuer paper route, not a statewide rule for every signer or informational/digital output. SOS FAQ 3 specifically addresses birth/death records, not a universal marriage countersignature requirement.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: San Mateo Birth and Death Certificates, marriage sentence; SOS FAQ 3; mail item 1
routeFacts.evidence: issuer-specific instruction plus Notary Geek scope limit

routeFacts.claim: San Mateo accepts mailed certified-copy applications with the applicable notarized statement, return address and payment by preprinted U.S.-bank check or money order. Its current linked form and general-public fee table both list $19. Copies return by regular mail or a supplied prepaid overnight envelope. Record procurement is separate from SOS submission and return.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Marriage Certificates mail paragraphs; linked form pp1–3; fee table; SOS mail instructions
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer-procedure plus Notary Geek stage distinction

routeFacts.claim: CDPH FAQ 24 lists a foreign notary with an apostille as one application-notarization option. San Mateo marriage ordering instructions instead exclude acknowledgments by notaries outside the USA and specify listed U.S. consular officials or a qualifying foreign court judge. Obtain issuer-specific application instructions; do not transfer one office rule to another.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: CDPH FAQ 24; San Mateo overseas acknowledgment paragraph
routeFacts.evidence: different issuer procedures; no statewide harmonization inferred

routeFacts.claim: San Diego expressly labels its gold-seal marriage keepsake a souvenir, even though a confidential keepsake mail request needs a notarized statement. A keepsake, request application, scan or private copy is not the issuer-certified marriage record. Online ordering also does not establish apostille acceptance of a customer printout.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Keepsake souvenir notice; record ordering channels; SOS mail item 1
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer facts plus Notary Geek output distinction

routeFacts.claim: CDPH FAQ 25 instructs applicants to state apostille as the certified-copy request purpose and says further SOS instructions will follow. This does not say CDPH itself issues the apostille or that the record-order fee includes it. FAQ 5 says CDPH does not issue digital, scanned or faxed vital-record images.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: FAQ 5 and 25; SOS mail instructions
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer guidance plus Notary Geek competent-authority distinction

routeFacts.claim: A county no-record letter, CDPH CNPR and private eligibility affidavit are different evidence. The recipient determines its document requirements. An apostille authenticates official signature/capacity/seal; official capacity is not the applicant's legal capacity to marry.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: County heading; CDPH FAQ 6–7; State Requirements/Affidavit; SOS FAQ 1
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

routeFacts.claim: San Diego publishes a Letter of No Record request using its marriage application, full name and date of birth, marked LNR. No sworn statement or notarization is required. Mail costs $19 per letter by check/money order; another person can request in person for someone abroad.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: By Mail and third-party FAQ; application p.1 LNR exception
routeFacts.evidence: official-issuer-guidance

routeFacts.claim: San Diego holds marriage records for licenses issued in that county. A no-record result depends on supplied information. The public LNR procedure does not specify all searched years, name variants or confidential indexes; neither their inclusion nor exclusion is established. Its broad single-status wording is not adopted as proof of statewide or worldwide absence.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Record opening/General Info/license-county FAQ; LNR opening; form p.1
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

routeFacts.claim: CDPH FAQ 6–7 defines CNPR as a certified unsuccessful search using application information; the fee is retained. A record not yet in its database can yield CNPR. CDPH does not maintain confidential marriages and has published year gaps. No reviewed procedure establishes a comprehensive person-wide single-status search.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: FAQ 6–7,22; Copies of Vital Records; marriage availability/confidential paragraph
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

routeFacts.claim: The reviewed county application is not an issued-letter specimen. Exact no-record certifier, seal, paper output and any intermediate certification remain unresolved for San Diego LNR and CDPH CNPR. SOS general original-document rules do not approve an unseen letter or customer printout. Its birth/death exception and San Diego other signature services establish no automatic LNR step.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Application pp.1–2; FAQ 7; SOS mail item 1 and FAQ 3; county signature-service sections
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

routeFacts.claim: A recipient-accepted private single-status affidavit remains the declarant's assertion. California jurat wording does not certify truth, accuracy or validity. For a lawful California notarization the apostille target is the California notary; a different jurisdiction's official signature does not become Californian through the signer's residence.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Jurat disclaimer; SOS authority opening and FAQ 1; Affidavit of eligibility to marry
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

routeFacts.claim: San Diego's letter confirming the existence of a confidential marriage is positive evidence, distinct from a Letter of No Record. A prior divorce judgment concerns a prior marriage and does not by itself establish absence of a later marriage or all requirements for a new marriage.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: Confidential section; application p.1; Requirements for marriage abroad
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

routeFacts.claim: San Diego LNR procurement and SOS authentication are separate stages and fees. VIT720 asks for return name/address and contact details; published LNR material supplies no tracked-return or end-to-end deadline guarantee. SOS separately requires its eligible document, destination cover, fee and return arrangements.
routeFacts.sourceLocator: County By Mail; form p.2; SOS mail items 1–4
routeFacts.evidence: official guidance plus Notary Geek route inference

documentBranches.question: Which public official signed the birth/death certified copy?
documentBranches.route: If county clerk/recorder or State Registrar, follow the directly recognized signature path. For health officer/local registrar, check whether county clerk certification or a different certified copy is needed.

documentBranches.question: Is the document an original with a California notarial act, and which notary signature is to be authenticated?
documentBranches.route: Use the California notary signature route; do not describe the apostille as validation of the private document's underlying facts.

documentBranches.question: Was the public record issued or notarized outside California, or issued by a federal agency?
documentBranches.route: Identify the actual official signature and its designated authority before selecting a state/federal route. A California mailing address or requester does not make a foreign-origin official signature California's.

documentBranches.question: Can the original/certified physical document and cover sheet be mailed to Sacramento?
documentBranches.route: Use the carrier-specific Sacramento address, $20 per Apostille, and a return envelope with prepaid tracking postage if tracking is required. Overnight transport changes transit, not queue priority.

documentBranches.question: Can someone present the eligible original/certified document at Sacramento or Los Angeles?
documentBranches.route: Check current office location/hours, destination-country cover sheet, $20 per Apostille, and $6 per different official signature. A third party can submit on someone's behalf.

documentBranches.question: Is the requested item an SOS-issued certified filing or certificate of status for a corporation, LLC or LP, rather than a plain downloaded image?
documentBranches.route: Identify certified filing versus status certificate. For online output, hold paper-presentation acceptance pending an output-specific SOS answer; do not infer it from verification. Supported alternative: request an agency-issued certified copy/certificate on the paper order form, preserve all certification pages, then submit that actual certified record for apostille.
documentBranches.issuer: California Secretary of State, Business Programs Division
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Official signature on the SOS certification, not the company officer signature within the filed document
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Agency-issued certified record; exact customer-printed online-certified output acceptance unresolved
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: SOS record certification is required for the official-copy route; no private custodian notarization substituted
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Record procurement and apostille return are separate stages; paper orders mailed back or drop-off pickup as specified by the order form

documentBranches.question: Is this an operating agreement or bylaws maintained by the entity rather than a state filing?
documentBranches.route: Follow the actual California notary signature if privately notarized, not the California SOS filing route; company status alone does not authenticate a private document.

documentBranches.question: Does the recipient require an institutional academic record, and does the issuing registrar offer an apostille preparation/notarization package?
documentBranches.route: Obtain the issuer-prepared record/certification and original California notarial package; preserve attachments and submit through SOS. Follow the particular institution procedure, not a generic rule for every public or private school.
documentBranches.issuer: Issuing institution/registrar; UC Davis, UC Berkeley and Caltech are documented examples
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: California notary signature on the issuer-prepared package; registrar certification supplies academic-record provenance
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Issuer-approved record or diploma copy with completed original notarial/certification package; a bare photocopy or emailed scan of notarization is not established as accepted
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: Institution certification followed by California notarization in the cited examples; no county-clerk step is prescribed by those examples, and exceptional signer/output questions remain open
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section
documentBranches.returnConstraint: UC Davis offers mail or authorized pickup; Caltech describes forwarding to SOS and SOS return to requester. Confirm destination/return and any sealed-envelope requirement with issuer/recipient.

documentBranches.question: Is the presented document the student/custodian statement rather than issuer certification?
documentBranches.route: Label it as a private statement. Follow the California notary signature only if that is the requested document; do not substitute it for the issuer-certified academic record or imply recipient acceptance.
documentBranches.issuer: Student or other declarant, not the academic records issuer
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: California notary signature on the private statement
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Original properly notarized statement; an attached academic copy retains its separate provenance
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: Private declarant notarization does not supply registrar certification
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State for the California notary signature
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Standard SOS return rules apply; separate recipient confirmation needed for a private-statement substitute

documentBranches.question: Is the record only electronic, or is direct authentication of a school official signature proposed without notarization?
documentBranches.route: Keep exact output and signer acceptance unresolved. Obtain issuer-specific and SOS instructions; use the documented registrar notarization/paper package where available. Online ordering, a verification code, or an institutional no-apostille-needed statement is not recipient evidence.
documentBranches.issuer: Actual school/registrar identified on the record
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Proposed school official signature or electronic certification must be identified; no universal direct route established
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Exact electronic-to-paper and direct-school-signature presentation unresolved
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: Do not invent a county step or use a private copy statement as issuer certification
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California SOS only for an eligible California public-official signature; other-state/federal issuer requires its own authority
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Resolve output before selecting mail/counter; check recipient sealed-record requirements separately

documentBranches.question: Does the recipient need the actual California Superior Court decree/judgment and which certification/signature is on it?
documentBranches.route: Order the specified filed judgment and attachments as a court-issued certified paper copy. Identify the court certifier, date, seal and completeness. If the actual signature/output is confirmed acceptable to SOS, submit the original court-certified package. If not established, resolve CA-Q2 before claiming the route is ready; do not substitute a private notarized copy.
documentBranches.issuer: Originating California Superior Court; not CDPH for the decree
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Named court official signing the certification or accepted court authentication package, not merely a party signature or the judge name printed in the underlying judgment
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Court-issued certified paper package; customer printout of an electronic court certification unresolved
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: Court certification required for the certified-record route. Additional court countersignature/replacement or other intermediate step depends on actual SOS-recognized signer; no universal County Clerk requirement established.
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State for the eligible California court-official signature; federal court records are separate
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Obtain court-issued package first. Orange online/mail/telephone orders are mailed; access restrictions and source timing conflict apply. SOS return is a separate stage.

documentBranches.question: Is exemplification required by the recipient or specifically directed for the actual signature chain?
documentBranches.route: Obtain the issuing court authentication/exemplification package when needed. Preserve each court attestation; inspect the final signer and resolve SOS recognition. Orange and Stanislaus illustrate different court products, not a uniform statewide mandate.
documentBranches.issuer: Originating Superior Court
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: The specific court-official signature SOS will authenticate; identify it from the complete package
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Court-issued complete certification/exemplification with required signatures/seal; no self-printed equivalent established
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: Stanislaus G003 example: deputy attestation -> judge authentication -> deputy authentication of judge. This is an optional local court form, not proof the chain is always needed or sufficient for SOS.
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State for eligible California court-official signature
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Court procurement and SOS submission/return are separate; recipient may require exemplification independently of SOS authentication

documentBranches.issuer: California Secretary of State, Business Programs Division
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Official signature on the SOS certification, not the company officer signature within the filed document
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: SOS record certification is required for the official-copy route; no private custodian notarization substituted
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Record procurement and apostille return are separate stages; paper orders mailed back or drop-off pickup as specified by the order form
documentBranches.question: Is this only a free business image, plain copy or ordinary printout without SOS certification?
documentBranches.route: Obtain the requested SOS-certified filing; do not promote a plain image or private copy statement into an official certification.
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Not yet an agency-certified record

documentBranches.issuer: California Secretary of State, Business Programs Division
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Official signature on the SOS certification, not the company officer signature within the filed document
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: SOS record certification is required for the official-copy route; no private custodian notarization substituted
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Record procurement and apostille return are separate stages; paper orders mailed back or drop-off pickup as specified by the order form
documentBranches.question: Is this the complete SOS online-certified output or a customer print of it?
documentBranches.route: Preserve the complete certification and verification data; resolve CA-Q1 before asserting paper eligibility. Paper procurement is available, but neither automatic printout acceptance nor categorical rejection is established.
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Online-certified record; exact customer printout eligibility unresolved

documentBranches.issuer: California Secretary of State, Business Programs Division
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Official signature on the SOS certification, not the company officer signature within the filed document
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: SOS record certification is required for the official-copy route; no private custodian notarization substituted
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State, Notary Public Section
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Record procurement and apostille return are separate stages; paper orders mailed back or drop-off pickup as specified by the order form
documentBranches.question: Is this the complete agency-issued paper certified copy or certificate?
documentBranches.route: Inspect actual certification/signature and all pages; submit through SOS only when the returned record fits its signed/certified-document requirements. No private notary copy statement substitutes for SOS certification.
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Actual agency-issued paper certified record, subject to document inspection

documentBranches.question: Did a California notary alone purport to certify the academic copy, without an issuer certification or separate lawful declarant statement?
documentBranches.route: Do not treat the presented notary-only copy certification as an eligible academic-record package. Obtain the issuer certification/notarization route. Any lawful student/custodian declaration would be a newly prepared, different private document and requires separate recipient acceptance.
documentBranches.issuer: Purported notary-only copy certificate; academic issuer provenance is missing
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: No supported academic copy-certification act established by the presented certificate
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Presented notary-only academic copy certification is not supported; replace through the issuer or a separately authorized lawful document route
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: A notary stamp cannot supply absent issuer certification or create an unstated declarant affidavit
documentBranches.competentAuthority: Do not submit as an established California apostille route
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Resolve the unsupported certificate before any agency submission

documentBranches.question: Is a registered public marriage record required, and is the requester eligible for an authorized copy?
documentBranches.route: Use the license-issuing County Recorder, or CDPH for a confirmed available year. Ask for the certified marriage record for apostille use; inspect the certifier and complete paper output. Use the documented issuer route or confirm the exact signer before submission. An authorized copy does not establish recipient acceptance.
documentBranches.issuer: License-issuing County Recorder or CDPH-VR
documentBranches.authenticatedSignature: Official certifier on the issued marriage record, not the applicant or application notary
documentBranches.acceptedOutput: Issuer-issued certified paper marriage record; eligibility and actual signer/output must be established
documentBranches.intermediateCertification: No blanket marriage county countersignature is established; San Mateo has a specific direct route
documentBranches.competentAuthority: California Secretary of State for the qualifying California official signature
documentBranches.returnConstraint: Obtain the record through its issuer first; SOS return is a separate stage. Recipient acceptance and required delivery condition are not established.

documentBranches.question: Is the requester a party to the confidential marriage or entitled by court order?
documentBranches.route: Obtain the certified record from the County Clerk where the license was issued, using that office access and application rules. CDPH does not hold it. If access is not established, use marriage-confidential-access; do not substitute a public-record eligibility rule. Inspect the issued certifier/output before the SOS stage.
documentBranches.issuer: County Clerk where the confidential license was issued

documentBranches.returnConstraint: Issuer procurement and SOS return are separate. Preserve the issued package; recipient acceptance, required record age and delivery form must be established separately.

Recheck fees, forms, office notices and processing at use time; the October 28 observation of the October 27 queue page is not a deadline.

doNotInfer: A California Apostille proves the document's substantive content or guarantees recipient acceptance.
Any California birth or death certificate signature can be apostilled directly without checking the official's title.
The $6 counter charge applies to each document or to mailed requests.
An overnight mail package or prepaid return label speeds the agency's processing queue.
Los Angeles accepts mailed apostille requests.
California's use of one Apostille output for every foreign destination eliminates all additional outside-Convention requirements.
A valid bizfile verification code makes a customer-printed certified PDF eligible for apostille.
A private bylaws document becomes an SOS filing because its company has a status certificate.
A California certificate about a foreign-qualified company authenticates the separate formation record issued by another state.
A notarized student education statement is the university certified record.
A registrar-approved diploma-copy input means a bare photocopy can be sent to SOS.
Every public-school registrar signature can be apostilled directly without notarization.
Government Code 27201.1 supplies general apostille eligibility for printed electronic records.
CDPH Certificate of Record is the divorce decree or establishes finality.
Every court judgment requires County Clerk certification or judge-signed exemplification.
Every court deputy signature is directly recognized by SOS.
Online court ordering establishes acceptance of a customer-printed electronically certified court record.
Third-party SOS submission permission authorizes access to a confidential marriage record.
Informational public-marriage copies are uncertified, or an apostille removes their identity-use restriction.
A marriage-record application notarized outside California sends the resulting California certified record to that notary state.
A county-issued gold-seal keepsake is the certified marriage record.
SOS birth/death FAQ 3 imposes a universal marriage County Clerk intermediate step.
San Mateo direct paper route approves every informational, electronic or other-county marriage record.
A county no-record letter or CDPH CNPR establishes never-married or present worldwide marital status.
An apostille's reference to official capacity establishes the holder's capacity to marry.
San Diego requires notarization of its LNR application, or its $19 fee includes apostille.
Confidential indexes and all name/year variants are included or excluded in a San Diego LNR without evidence.

unresolvedQuestions.question: For a bizfileOnline-certified filing copy or certificate of status for a corporation, LLC or LP, will the Notary Public Section accept the customer-printed, complete unaltered PDF in its mail and counter apostille lanes? Which signature/certification pages, seal, verification identifier and printing conditions are required? If not, which agency-issued paper certification should be ordered on the March 2026 form?
unresolvedQuestions.supportedAlternative: Use the published paper certified-record order procedure and preserve the agency certification; inspect the returned output before apostille submission.

unresolvedQuestions.agency: California SOS Notary Public Section and originating Superior Court
unresolvedQuestions.question: For a paper Superior Court judgment certified by a named deputy clerk with date and court seal, can SOS authenticate that signature directly? If not, what exact court countersignature, replacement or intermediate certification is required? Is judge-signed exemplification an SOS requirement for this signer or solely a recipient requirement? Is any County Clerk step necessary? What specific paper presentation of electronically certified court records is accepted?
unresolvedQuestions.supportedAlternative: Request the originating court certified paper record and identify its certifier; obtain an accepted court-issued signature chain when needed. Do not notarize a private photocopy as a substitute.

unresolvedQuestions.agency: California SOS Notary Public Section and issuing registrar
unresolvedQuestions.question: Which California public-school registrar signatures, if any, are authenticated directly? For issuer-prepared notarized records, what original paper certification and attachments are required, and is any additional official certification needed for the identified signer? How should an electronically issued transcript/diploma be presented, and can the issuer supply a paper counterpart consistent with recipient sealed-envelope requirements?
unresolvedQuestions.supportedAlternative: Use the issuing institution published registrar-certification/notarization route and original package; obtain recipient requirements separately.

unresolvedQuestions.agency: California SOS Notary Public Section and issuing marriage-record custodian
unresolvedQuestions.question: For the named marriage-record certifier and complete proposed output, is direct authentication available, or is a specific issuer countersignature or replacement required? Does SOS accept this certified informational copy or exact electronic-to-paper presentation? The separate recipient must establish whether that copy type and delivery form meet its requirements.
unresolvedQuestions.supportedAlternative: Use a lawfully obtained issuer-issued authorized paper marriage certificate when that is the required record; San Mateo publishes a direct route for its Clerk-Recorder certificates. Other signer/output conditions remain subject to confirmation.

unresolvedQuestions.agency: San Diego Recorder/County Clerk and California SOS Notary Public Section
unresolvedQuestions.question: Which indexes, date ranges, names/aliases and confidential-record classes does the LNR search cover, and what registration lag/limits does its issued text state? Which official title, signature and seal appear? Does SOS accept that intact paper output directly, or require identified intermediate certification? Are any electronic copies or customer printouts accepted?
unresolvedQuestions.supportedAlternative: Use the published county LNR procurement route when the recipient wants that search scope; retain the issued result and hold SOS submission until exact signer/output is resolved.

unresolvedQuestions.agency: CDPH Vital Records and California SOS Notary Public Section
unresolvedQuestions.question: Does CDPH offer a person-based no-marriage search distinct from an unsuccessful certified-copy application? If so, what years, identifiers and record classes, application, fee, attestation, certifier and paper output apply? For an actual CNPR, what signature and intermediate certification does SOS require, including any electronic-to-paper conditions?
unresolvedQuestions.supportedAlternative: Read an existing CNPR only within its documented search limits. Use the specifically researched county procurement procedure if that is the recipient-requested evidence; a private affidavit is a separate recipient-dependent route.
